From 6026685de33b0db5b2b6b0e9b41b3a1a3261033c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Disseldorp <ddiss@suse.de>
Date: Wed, 3 May 2017 17:39:08 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] cifs: fix CIFS_ENUMERATE_SNAPSHOTS oops

As with 618763958b22, an open directory may have a NULL private_data
pointer prior to readdir. CIFS_ENUMERATE_SNAPSHOTS must check for this
before dereference.

Fixes: 834170c85978 ("Enable previous version support")
Signed-off-by: David Disseldorp <ddiss@suse.de>
CC: Stable <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Steve French <smfrench@gmail.com>

diff --git a/fs/cifs/ioctl.c b/fs/cifs/ioctl.c
index 7f4bba574930..4d598a71cf84 100644
--- a/fs/cifs/ioctl.c
+++ b/fs/cifs/ioctl.c
@@ -213,6 +213,8 @@ long cifs_ioctl(struct file *filep, unsigned int command, unsigned long arg)
 			rc = smb_mnt_get_fsinfo(xid, tcon, (void __user *)arg);
 			break;
 		case CIFS_ENUMERATE_SNAPSHOTS:
+			if (pSMBFile == NULL)
+				break;
 			if (arg == 0) {
 				rc = -EINVAL;
 				goto cifs_ioc_exit;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `fs/cifs/ioctl.c`**
   - A check was added to verify if `pSMBFile` is `NULL` before proceeding with the `CIFS_ENUMERATE_SNAPSHOTS` case in the `cifs_ioctl` function. If `pSMBFile` is `NULL`, the function will break out of the case without attempting to dereference it.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification addresses a potential bug where dereferencing a `NULL` pointer (`pSMBFile`) could lead to a system crash (oops). By adding the check for `NULL`, the patch ensures that the function safely exits without attempting to access invalid memory, thus preventing the crash. This change is related to a previous fix (identified by the commit hash) that also aimed to improve the handling of snapshot enumeration in the CIFS filesystem.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
struct cifsFileInfo *pSMBFile = filep->private_data;
...
tcon = tlink_tcon(pSMBFile->tlink);
```
Reason:
When an open directory has a `NULL` pointer for `private_data`, dereferencing it in the assignment `tcon = tlink_tcon(pSMBFile->tlink);` will result in a crash due to attempting to access an invalid memory location.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (pSMBFile == NULL)
    break;
```
Reason:
By adding this check before dereferencing `pSMBFile`, the code now safely exits the switch case in `CIFS_ENUMERATE_SNAPSHOTS` without attempting to access `tcon`, thereby preventing a potential crash when the `private_data` pointer is `NULL`.
